thread:
anya: late-night quick QA — noticed a weird interaction between stop sequences and max_tokens in canary. when a stop triggers mid-token we sometimes get no logprobs and the response can exceed max_tokens. anyone else seen this? :eyes:

jordan: can you paste the exact request (model + params) and whether streaming was on? small repro helps.

anya: yup, minimal repro below:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","input":"List items:\n1.","max_tokens":5,"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"stop":["\\n\\n"]}'
```
streaming: false. prompt ends with a partial token after the period. response sometimes returns 7 tokens and the "logprobs" field is null for the last chunk.

lee: hm. runtime semantics: stop seq is applied at decode boundary, but our tokenizer can split what humans see as a newline into multiple subtokens. if stop matches mid-subtoken we currently finish the token before checking max_tokens enforcement. that could explain >max_tokens. logprobs null if we drop the token in post-processing due to stop truncate.

mira: is that a regression? I thought we enforced max_tokens at the decoder level.

anya: only seeing it on the canary pool (dedicated canary nodes). prod and local didn't show it.

jordan: tagging runtime infra — @janet can you take a look? add a unit test for stop matching on subtoken boundaries and for logprobs when stop truncates.

janet: on it. I can repro with your curl. quick plan: 1) add test that forces stop mid-token, 2) ensure max_tokens clamps at decoder output count, 3) preserve logprobs for the final emitted token even if we later trim by stop. will push a hotfix to canary if it matches. :memo:

anya: thanks! small priority note: if we preserve logprobs for trimmed token, make sure SDK still doesn't surface tokens beyond stop in streaming mode. we want consistent behavior between streaming and non-streaming.

lee: good call. streaming pipeline has a different postproc hook so add integration test for both.

janet: will do. ping me if you hit a deterministic seed that always repros.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: build/2026-03-15-03:21 started by @janet :rocket: (tracking: #canary-2026-03-15).

anya: I'll hold off on the canary QA checklist until you confirm the fix. thanks all. :thumbsup:
